title: Four lifecycle events fire with metadata-only payloads and no event body carries a secret
asA: operator whose observability sink carries the Hetzner lifecycle trail
iWant: the provisioner facade to fire the four lifecycle events (provisionerReady, hetznerServerProvisioned, hetznerSnapshotTaken, hetznerServerDestroyed) with metadata-only payloads and no secret content
soThat: the observability sink carries the operational trail without ever leaking a token or an ssh key

acceptanceCriteria.description: hcloud-dry-run-mock.mjs drives every lifecycle event through the facade against a mocked hcloud shim; the accumulated event stream carries only the metadata fields named on REQ-006; a mutation SIMULATE_EVENT_SECRECY_LEAK=true injects the token into the hetznerServerProvisioned payload and the probe FAILS with a defensive-fake finding naming the leaked field.

Secret exclusion by grep-across-source. Given the fixture provisioner source and the fixture renderer source (per TAC-3803), when a source-tree scan searches every onEvent call site and every event-record construction site for the substring HETZNER_ACCOUNT_API_KEY and any ssh key body, then no match is found; a mutation SIMULATE_EVENT_TOKEN_LEAK=true adds the token into an event field and the probe FAILS naming the leaked field.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the fixture provisioner and renderer source, and the four documented lifecycle events
acceptanceCriteria.when: a source-tree grep runs across every event-record construction site
acceptanceCriteria.then: no HETZNER_ACCOUNT_API_KEY or ssh-key-body match is found; the mutation FAILS naming the leaked field

acceptanceCriteria.description: Event fires once per lifecycle moment (repeat-run idempotency). Given a completed provision and a completed destroy, when the run replays a second time against the same manifest and account, then hetznerServerProvisioned fires once per successful create and hetznerServerDestroyed fires once per successful destroy; no duplicate event fires for a run whose upstream call did not change resource state.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the run replays a second time against the same manifest and account
acceptanceCriteria.then: each lifecycle event fires exactly once per successful state change; no duplicate event fires on a no-op call
